edges.reason: Sorted input removes the hash map — two pointers suffice when random access is free.
Inverts the lookup direction: store previously seen numbers and query by complement.
At-Most-Two-Distinct generalises the two-pointer invariant from unique chars to a 2-char frequency cap.
At-Most-K-Distinct further generalises to an arbitrary k-character frequency cap.
Minimum Window Substring adds a coverage requirement — the window shrinks only when all required chars are covered.
Longest Palindromic Subsequence lifts the contiguous constraint into a 2-D DP on substring boundaries.
Palindromic Substrings counts all palindromic windows using the same expand-from-centre scan.
Reduces 3Sum to 2Sum on the sorted tail for each fixed first element.
3Sum Closest uses the same sorted two-pointer scan but tracks the nearest sum instead of an exact match.
4Sum wraps a second fixed element around the same 3Sum two-pointer kernel.
Generate Parentheses uses backtracking to produce all valid strings whose validity mirrors the stack check in #20.
Longest Valid Parentheses reuses stack-based matching but extends it to track the start index of each valid window.
Merge K Lists applies the two-list merge pairwise via a min-heap or divide-and-conquer tournament.
Sort List reduces to merge sort whose merge step is exactly #21 applied to two linked-list halves.
Smallest Range Covering K Lists advances the same k-way heap frontier, tracking the window span instead of emitting nodes.
Remove Duplicates II allows two occurrences — the write-pointer logic widens from k=1 to k=2.
Reuses stack-based parenthesis matching, then tracks substring boundaries to maximize valid length.
Find Minimum in Rotated Array removes the target comparison and seeks the break point directly.
Find First and Last Position runs two separate binary searches for the left and right bounds.
Adds the no-reuse constraint: sort + skip duplicates in the DFS to avoid revisiting the same candidate.
Combination Sum IV counts ordered sequences — the counting version is a 1D knapsack DP rather than backtracking.
Restricts candidates to 1-9 with a fixed count, changing only the range passed to DFS.
Both use a decreasing monotonic stack; #42 counts horizontal water while #84 computes a maximal rectangle width.
Trapping Rain Water II fills a 2-D basin — the monotonic stack becomes a min-heap flooding inward from the border.
Permutations II has duplicates — sort and skip same-value elements at the same recursion level.
N-Queens II only counts solutions, so the same diagonal-conflict DFS increments a counter instead of materialising boards.
Sudoku Solver is the same constraint-propagation backtracking: place, check conflicts, recurse, undo.
Spiral Matrix II fills the spiral instead of reading it — same boundary-shrink loop in reverse.
Spiral Matrix III generates coordinates in spiral order starting from an arbitrary origin.
Jump Game II asks for the minimum jumps — greedy farthest-reach becomes a BFS level counter.
Jump Game III adds backward jumps and a target, turning the greedy into BFS reachability.
Spiral Matrix III walks off-grid, so the boundary-shrink loop becomes a step-length-growing walk with bounds checks.
Adds obstacles: cells with obstacles get dp=0; the rest use the same transition.
Unique Paths III requires visiting every empty cell exactly once, needing backtracking over the DP count.
Unique Paths III must visit every empty cell exactly once, so the DP table gives way to exhaustive backtracking.
Min Cost Climbing Stairs adds a cost per stair — the Fibonacci recurrence gains a min() overlay.
Search a 2D Matrix II loses the fully-sorted-flattening property, so the search walks from a corner instead of halving.
Subsets II has duplicate elements — sort and skip the same element at the same DFS depth to de-dup.
Word Search II replaces single-word DFS with trie-guided search for all words simultaneously.
Minesweeper floods the same 4/8-neighbour grid DFS, but reveals cells instead of matching a word.
Remove Duplicates from Sorted List II deletes all duplicates rather than keeping one representative.
Maximal Rectangle reduces each row to a histogram and applies the #84 stack algorithm per row.
Reverse in k-groups repeatedly applies the m-to-n reversal across non-overlapping windows of size k.
Level Order II reverses the output — append to a deque front instead of the back.
Right Side View keeps only the last node per level from a standard BFS traversal.
Find Largest Value in Each Row tracks the per-level maximum rather than the full level list.
Path Sum II collects all valid paths rather than a boolean — accumulate the path list in DFS.
Path Sum III counts any-start paths — a prefix-sum hash map avoids the O(n^2) re-traversal.
Pascal's Triangle II needs only row k, so the O(n^2) table collapses to one rolling row.
Unlimited transactions turns the problem into summing every positive price delta.
Adds a cooldown day — the greedy accumulation from II becomes a DP on hold/sold/cooldown states.
Adds a per-transaction fee — same unlimited-transaction structure but subtract fee on each sell.
At-most-2 transactions splits into a forward pass for the first and a backward pass for the second.
At-most-2 transactions can no longer be greedy — split into a forward and a backward best-profit pass.
Generalises the 2-transaction DP to k transactions by tracking localmax per transaction count.
Valid Palindrome II allows one deletion — greedily skip the mismatching character and re-check each side.
Word Ladder II records all shortest-path predecessors via BFS, then reconstructs all paths with DFS.
Clone Graph traverses the same adjacency structure but builds a copy instead of counting components.
Missing Number can also be solved by XOR-ing indices against values — same self-cancelling-pairs invariant.
Linked List Cycle II extends Floyd's two-pointer to locate the exact entry node of the cycle.
Min Stack pairs main + aux stacks — same dual-structure O(1) trick as the hash-map + list in LRU.
Insert Delete GetRandom pairs a hash map with a dynamic array to achieve O(1) for all three operations.
Reverse Words II must work in place — reverse the whole array, then reverse each word.
With duplicates the invariant weakens: a middle equal to right forces r-- before the halving.
Majority Element II runs two simultaneous Boyer-Moore counters, since up to two elements can exceed n/3.
Reverse Words III reverses the letters inside each word while keeping word order, the exact inverse of II.
Power of Two is the n & (n-1) == 0 special case of the clear-lowest-set-bit trick used to count bits.
Counting Bits caches results for every i < n, replacing the per-number loop with dp[i] = dp[i >> 1] + (i & 1).
Circular arrangement means either the first or last house is excluded — run linear DP twice on the two sub-arrays.
Tree layout replaces the linear chain with DFS post-order: rob node vs. rob both children.
Both count connected components; the grid's implicit 4-neighbour adjacency becomes an explicit adjacency matrix.
Same component count on an explicit edge list rather than an implicit grid.
Reverse sublist [m,n] by inserting each node after the anchor rather than reversing the whole list.
Course Schedule II returns the topological order itself, not just feasibility.
Add and Search Word extends the trie with wildcard '.' that fans out DFS across all children.
Word Search II preloads all words into a trie and prunes the 2-D DFS early on trie misses.
House Robber III replaces the circular array with a tree — the two DP states become a post-order return pair.
Kth Largest in a Stream cannot re-partition on each insert, so quickselect gives way to a bounded size-k min-heap.
Combination Sum IV counts ordered sequences, so backtracking over combinations is replaced by a 1-D counting DP.
Contains Duplicate II adds a window constraint k — maintain a sliding-window hash set of the last k elements.
Contains Duplicate III relaxes equality to a value window t — bucket by v // t so neighbours land in adjacent buckets.
Basic Calculator II drops parentheses but adds * and /, so precedence is handled by peeking at the stack top instead of recursing.
Basic Calculator III combines the precedence handling of II with the parenthesis recursion of I.
Shortest Word Distance II precomputes position lists and merges them with a two-pointer scan per query.
Shortest Word Distance III handles word1 == word2 by tracking the previous seen index of the same word.
Meeting Rooms II counts concurrent meetings rather than detecting any overlap — sort starts and ends separately.
Both sort intervals by start and sweep; merge combines overlaps while Meeting Rooms II counts them.
Palindrome Permutation II generates all such strings — half-frequency halves are permuted by backtracking.
Wiggle Sort II requires strict inequality — median-partition + index-mapping avoids a full O(n log n) sort.
Inorder Successor II has parent pointers — climb toward root instead of descending from it.
Sliding Window Median keeps the same two-heap median invariant but must also evict elements leaving the window.
Russian Doll Envelopes sorts by (width asc, height desc) to reduce the 2-D problem to a 1-D LIS.
Range Sum Query 2D extends the 1-D prefix array to a 2-D prefix table with inclusion-exclusion queries.
Range Sum Query Mutable replaces the static prefix array with a Binary Indexed Tree for O(log n) updates.
Coin Change 2 counts the number of ways rather than the minimum — unbounded knapsack counting DP.
Both fill a capacity-indexed DP table; coin change minimises count while subset-sum only asks reachability.
Graph Valid Tree adds the acyclic + single-component check: exactly n-1 edges and one component.
Reverse String II reverses every-other k-sized block — apply the same two-pointer to a sliding window.
Top K Frequent Words is the same count-then-select-k problem with a lexicographic tiebreak on equal frequency.
Intersection II counts duplicates — use a frequency map instead of a set.
Find K Pairs walks a k-way merge frontier with a heap, exactly like merging k sorted lists.
Guess Number II pays the guessed value as a cost, turning a binary search into a minimax interval DP.
Target Sum rewrites +/- assignment as choosing a positive subset with a fixed sum — the same subset-sum DP.
Ones and Zeroes is subset-sum with two independent capacities, so the DP table gains a second dimension.
Path Sum IV encodes nodes numerically; reconstruct the tree first, then the same DFS applies.
Splits four lists into two pairs, hashes the pair sums, then queries by complement — two-pass 2Sum.
Max Consecutive Ones II allows one flip — a two-pointer window tracks at most one zero inside.
Max Consecutive Ones III generalises the one-flip window to k flips.
Next Greater Element II wraps the array circularly — iterate 2n indices with modulo on a monotonic stack.
Climbing Stairs counts two-step paths — recurrence is identical, dp[n] = F(n+1).
Game Play Analysis II extends from first-login to multi-date queries on the same player.
Lonely Pixel II adds a group constraint — a pixel qualifies only if its row set is consistent.
Maximum Average Subarray II lifts the fixed-length constraint — a sliding minimum + prefix-sum trick.
Both keep only the top k under a heap; frequency counting replaces raw values as the heap key.
Rotated Sorted Array has one break point — check which half is sorted to pick the correct side.
Search Insert Position adapts binary search to return the insertion index on a miss.
Basic Calculator IV carries symbolic variables, so the operand type becomes a polynomial rather than an int.
Sort Array By Parity II requires alternating positions — two write pointers, one per parity.
Smallest Range II pairs each element with +K or -K and finds the optimal split — greedy on sorted array.
Sales Analysis II adds a negative filter — exclude sellers who also sold a disallowed product.
Sales Analysis III further restricts to the first and last reporting period, adding a date range filter.
